state.case_summary:
A 32-year-old Han Chinese man, a professional driver, presented with a 4-year history of a slowly enlarging pigmented lesion on the upper left lip vermilion. He first noticed a 1 cm × 0.5 cm macule, which progressively increased in size without symptoms. After 3 years, he noted brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion. He had no significant medical or family history, and he did not smoke or drink.

On examination, multiple pigmented papules of various sizes involved the vermilion of the upper left lip, with brownish skin discoloration extending from 0.5 cm medial to the left angle of the mouth to the left philtral ridge. The lip was slightly swollen. Intraorally, a 1.5 cm lesion extended from the labial frenum to 0.5 cm medial to the left angle of the mouth; it was non-tender, non-indurated, and exhibited focal ulcerations. No cervical lymphadenopathy or other skin lesions were found.

Results of a complete blood count, biochemical profile, and urinalysis were within normal limits. Chest radiography was unremarkable. A computed tomography scan of the head and neck was performed to assess local extent of the lesion and to evaluate regional lymph nodes.
